figures.shows: Continuum flux densities of the East and West nuclei versus frequency from literature and this work, with reference power laws for non-thermal synchrotron and Rayleigh-Jeans blackbody emission.

readable_values: approx. West flux near 110 GHz about 0.03 Jy

figures.shows: Position-velocity strip maps along the major axes of the East (PA 50 deg) and West (PA 265 deg) nuclei showing rotating kinematics of the CO(1-0) emission.

approx. West peak near 5250 km/s at -0.1 arcsec
approx. West velocity range about 4800 to 5700 km/s
figures.caption_quote: Spatial-velocity strip maps along the major axes of Arp 220 East (PA=50◦) and West (PA = 265◦).

figures.shows: Derived rotation curves, enclosed dynamical mass, and face-on CO emissivity versus radius for the East and West disks from fitting high-resolution line profiles.
readable_values: approx. West peak rotation velocity about 750 km/s at about 5 pc
approx. West enclosed mass plateau about 0.8 x10^8 solar masses beyond 40 pc
approx. East rotation velocity about 300 km/s at 50 to 100 pc
approx. West central face-on emissivity about 5 mJy km/s pc^-2 at -75 pc
figures.caption_quote: A central point mass of 8 × 108 M⊙is required in the West nucleus and only a limit of < 108 M⊙in the East nucleus.

figures.shows: Model circular velocity curves for a central black hole plus an r^-2 disk, comparing the full disk integration with the spherical approximation, to illustrate non-spherical gravitational effects.
figures.validation_check: Illustrates that the spherical approximation for dynamical mass can differ from the proper disk circular velocity.
readable_values: approx. disk plus BH velocity peak about 380 km/s near 80 pc
approx. disk plus BH dip to about 170 km/s near 20 pc
approx. BH-only velocity about 150 km/s at 100 pc
figures.caption_quote: The circular velocities are shown for a mass distribution including a central point-mass (BH) of 5×108 M⊙, and disk of mass 109 M⊙distributed with an r−2 density falloff between 20 and 80 pc.

figures.shows: Estimated disk scale heights H(R) for the West and East disks (left) and the corresponding disk crossing or turbulent dissipation timescales (right) as functions of radius.
figures.validation_check: Derived H and dissipation timescales depend on the adopted velocity dispersions (109 and 52 km/s) and rotation curves.
readable_values: approx. West disk thickness about 40 pc at 80 pc radius
approx. East disk thickness about 20 pc at 120 pc radius
approx. West crossing time peak about 0.41 Myr at 80 pc
approx. East crossing time about 0.44 Myr at 120 pc
figures.caption_quote: The disk crossing timescale (H/σv(1d)) which is equivalent to the turbulent dissipation timescales calculated from Equation 4 with fa = 1.
